summary: As of mid-to-late 2026, ChatGPT/GPT-5 from OpenAI retains the largest consumer mindshare with 55.5% of generative AI web traffic, but its dominance has eroded significantly from 73.3% a year prior as Gemini surged to 25.6% and Claude reached 9.3%. Enterprise API usage tells a different story, with Anthropic leading at 40% of enterprise API spend versus OpenAI at 27% and Google at 21%. Open-weight models like Llama 4, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and Qwen3 have closed the benchmark gap to within a few points of frontier closed models, reshaping the self-hosted and cost-sensitive deployment market.

models.name: GPT-5
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT drives 55.5% of global generative AI web traffic as of August 2026 (Similarweb), and OpenAI leads LLM API provider rankings; GPT-5 is available on Azure OpenAI Service, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI, giving it unmatched aggregator reach across enterprise procurement channels.
strengths: Largest installed base and ecosystem
Strongest brand recognition among developers and enterprises
Available on all major cloud aggregators (Azure, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI)
Broad multimodal capabilities
Extensive plugin and tool-use ecosystem
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise deployments, consumer applications, and teams requiring maximum ecosystem compatibility

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google Gemini grew from 527.7 million to 2.9 billion monthly web visits between May 2025 and May 2026 (~450% growth per Similarweb), reaching 25.6% AI web traffic share in August 2026; natively integrated into Google Cloud Vertex AI and deeply embedded in Google Workspace, giving it massive enterprise aggregator reach.
strengths: Largest context window among top-tier models
Deep native integration with Google Cloud Vertex AI
Strong multimodal and code capabilities
Rapid release cadence keeping competitive with frontier labs
Built-in access to Google Search grounding
models.best_for: Long-document analysis, multimodal workflows, and Google Cloud-native enterprise applications

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5.1
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic leads enterprise API spend at 40% of the market per Menlo Ventures 2025, Claude reached 9.3% of AI web traffic (855% YoY growth) in August 2026, and Claude models are available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, making it the dominant enterprise API model despite lower consumer profile; Claude Fable 5.1 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 66 as of September 2026.
strengths: Leads enterprise API spend with 40% market share
Top benchmark scores on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex
Industry-leading instruction following and writing quality
Strong safety and constitutional AI design
models.best_for: Enterprise knowledge work, long-form writing, complex instruction following, and regulated-industry deployments

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Llama models consistently rank among the top downloads on HuggingFace and are the default open-weight choice cited across developer surveys; Llama 4 is available via AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex, giving it the broadest aggregator coverage of any open-weight model.
strengths: Broadest aggregator availability of any open-weight model
Zero licensing cost for self-hosted deployment
Massive HuggingFace download and fine-tuning community
Strong general reasoning benchmark performance
Flexible deployment: local, cloud, or on-premise
models.best_for: Self-hosted and on-premise enterprise deployments, fine-tuning for domain-specific use cases, and cost-sensitive production workloads

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek models accounted for 24.4% of text requests on OpenRouter in the week of September 21, 2026, making it the top model on the API aggregator developer marketplace; DeepSeek-V4-Pro leads the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard on SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench, and the broader DeepSeek family held 4.1% of AI web traffic as of May 2026.
strengths: Leads OpenRouter API marketplace with 24.4% of text requests
Top SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench scores among open models
Developed with significantly less compute cost than Western frontier models
Extremely competitive price-to-performance ratio
Strong open-weight alternative to closed frontier models
models.best_for: Coding assistance, software engineering automation, and cost-optimized API deployments requiring frontier-level code performance

models.name: Qwen3 (Qwen family)
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises across consumer electronics, gaming, and other sectors per Shakudo research; Qwen3.6-27B ranks among the top open-weight code generation models on the Onyx leaderboard, and the family is available through multiple cloud providers in Asia-Pacific and beyond.
strengths: Over 90,000 enterprise adoptions globally
Strong multilingual capabilities across Asian languages
Top-tier code generation in the open-weight category
Highly active HuggingFace community with numerous fine-tuned variants
Available in multiple size tiers for different compute budgets
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise applications, Asia-Pacific deployments, and teams needing strong open-weight code and reasoning models

models.name: Grok-3
models.popularity_notes: Grok held 2.4% of global AI web traffic in August 2026 (Similarweb) and is deeply integrated with the X platform giving it access to real-time social data; ranked among the top five AI LLMs of 2026 by multiple industry sources including SEOvision.
strengths: Real-time X/Twitter data integration and web search grounding
Strong performance on reasoning and math benchmarks
Unique access to real-time social media signal
Competitive benchmark scores vs. top-tier closed models
Growing enterprise API offering
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analytics, and applications requiring up-to-the-minute web grounding

models.name: Mistral Large / Mistral Small 4
models.popularity_notes: Mistral models are recommended as the top local/desktop LLM option in multiple 2026 developer guides and are available on Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI; Mistral Small 4 (119B MoE, Apache 2.0 licensed) launched March 2026 with strong instruct, reasoning, and coding performance at $0.15 input / $0.60 output, making it a high-adoption cost-optimized enterprise choice.
strengths: Best price-to-performance among European frontier models
Available on Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI
Apache 2.0 license for unrestricted commercial use
Strong instruct, reasoning, and coding in a single model
Top recommendation for local and desktop LLM deployments
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive production workloads, European data-sovereignty requirements, and local/edge deployments

models.name: GPT-6 Astra (GPT-5.1)
models.popularity_notes: GPT-5.1 is listed by Future AGI as part of OpenAI's continued API market leadership, and GPT-6 Astra is noted to beat Claude Fable 5.1 on the hardest math, reasoning, and cyber benchmarks as of September 2026; benefits from OpenAI's full aggregator presence across Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI.
strengths: Leads on hardest math, reasoning, and cybersecurity benchmarks
Inherits full OpenAI aggregator ecosystem
State-of-the-art performance for specialized high-difficulty tasks
Strong tool use and agentic workflow support
Backed by OpenAI's enterprise support infrastructure
models.best_for: Advanced reasoning, mathematical problem solving, cybersecurity research, and agentic AI pipelines requiring maximum capability

models.name: Microsoft Phi-4
models.popularity_notes: Phi-4 is cited in multiple 2026 open-source LLM surveys as the top choice for high-performance reasoning in small-scale and edge deployments; natively integrated into Azure AI and available through Azure OpenAI Service and IBM watsonx, giving it strong enterprise aggregator coverage disproportionate to its model size.
strengths: Best reasoning performance per parameter in the small-model category
Natively integrated into Azure AI and IBM watsonx
Extremely low inference cost for edge and on-device deployment
MIT licensed for unrestricted commercial use
Strong performance on STEM and structured reasoning tasks
models.best_for: Edge deployments, on-device AI, cost-optimized reasoning tasks, and Azure-native enterprise applications with tight latency budgets

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.popularity_notes: MiniMax M3 appears in the top five of the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard for both bug-fixing (SWE-bench) and code generation as of July 2026, clustering tightly with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K2.6 within a few benchmark points, indicating genuine adoption among performance-seeking developers rather than a clear drop-off from the top 10.
strengths: Top-five SWE-bench Verified and code generation scores among open models
Exceptionally large 1M token context window
Competitive price for frontier-adjacent performance
Rapidly rising adoption on API marketplaces like OpenRouter
Strong reasoning capabilities alongside coding
models.best_for: Long-context code review, large codebase analysis, and cost-effective frontier-adjacent API deployments
